page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The host utilizes Intel x86_64 processors running at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency. Compute resources consist of 64 physical cores delivering 128 dedicated vCPUs with two hardware threads per core. System memory is scaled to 1024 GB, establishing a standard memory-optimized ratio of 8 GB per vCPU.

Local storage is bundled directly onto the instance, providing 7600 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. This internal storage eliminates network overhead for intermediate data sets, temporary tables, and write-heavy logging operations. Network infrastructure provides 200 Gbps of baseline bandwidth, supporting high-throughput cluster synchronization and node interconnects without requiring complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural standpoint, the r8idn.32xlarge combines high CPU thread density, substantial memory footprint, and extensive local NVMe storage. Because the instance contains no dedicated GPU accelerators, resource density is focused strictly on general-purpose compute, memory capacity, and disk throughput. This resource allocation provides cost efficiency for memory-bound and disk-heavy enterprise applications compared to heterogeneous accelerator nodes. Primary operational targets include in-memory databases, high-volume transactional systems, distributed cache clusters, and intensive extract, transform, and load processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.32xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring extensive RAM and fast local storage. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 128 dedicated x86_64 virtual cores mapped to 64 physical Intel processor cores operating at up to 3.9 GHz, alongside 1024 GB of system memory. This hardware profile maintains an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio, catering to systems constrained by memory density. In addition to compute and memory, the instance incorporates 7600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, enabling low-latency data access without relying solely on network-attached volumes. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 200 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data replication and distributed cluster communication. The lack of hardware accelerators makes it cost-efficient for core CPU and storage pipelines rather than machine learning tasks. It is configured for in-memory databases, large cache layers, big data analytics, and real-time transaction processing.
